Executive summary

The luxury picture, briefly

The Diriyah ecosystem owns the loudest luxury-residential conversation in KSA Meta inventory, but almost none of that volume comes from Diriyah Company’s own page. DarGlobal’s Rayana Mansions / Amara campaign carries the ecosystem; Christie’s Real Estate Saudi adds broker-side polish; dar_al_omran adds an architecture-led narrative around the Wadi Safar Experience Center. Diriyah Company’s own page contributes a single direct sales creative for Armani Residences and four disclaimer-paused brand ads.

Red Sea Global is the only giga-developer running a coordinated luxury-residential push from its own page — the Nammos Residences at AMAALA launch (April 2026) and a steady Miraval The Red Sea Residences drumbeat. The Mandarin Oriental Jeddah Central announcement surfaces via the Branded Living editorial channel rather than the operator itself. Other branded operators in scope — Aman, Baccarat, Raffles, Chedi, Corinthia, Ritz-Carlton, Bvlgari, Six Senses, Four Seasons — are silent on Meta in KSA.

ROSHN’s luxury surface is narrow by design: only the Sedra branded-villa subset qualifies, and it is being sold almost entirely through one international broker (Expat Key Real Estate) running a tight Elie Saab-branded creative system at SAR 3.8M+. ROSHN’s own page is functionally absent from the luxury conversation.

Cluster 01

Diriyah Company ecosystem

Diriyah Company itself runs only one direct sales-led creative in the period — the Armani Residences “stitched in stone” ad. The remaining direct page output is awareness (TIME100 partnership) and four brand creatives that paused for missing required disclaimers despite reaching audiences over one million. The volume sits with the partner ecosystem: DarGlobal with the Amara at Rayana / Rayana Mansions push, Christie’s Real Estate Saudi with broker-led Rayana storytelling, dar_al_omran with the Wadi Safar Experience Center.

Cluster 02

ROSHN luxury — branded villas only

ROSHN is a mass-market developer; the part of their inventory that qualifies as luxury is the branded-villa subset of Sedra. Almost the entire active push for that tier comes from one broker, Expat Key Real Estate, running a tightly templated creative system that hits the Elie Saab Branded Villas at SAR 3.8M+ alongside rental and apartments tiers. ROSHN’s own page is functionally absent from luxury Meta advertising in the period.

Cluster 03

Red Sea Global luxury

Red Sea Global is the most active luxury-residential advertiser of the three giga-projects on Meta, splitting its push between the Nammos Residences at AMAALA launch (April 2026 sales window) and the evergreen Miraval The Red Sea Residences hospitality-and-ownership creative. Mandarin Oriental Jeddah Central has surfaced via the Branded Living editorial channel, but the operator itself is silent on Meta in KSA.

Cluster 04

Other luxury KSA residential

NEOM’s Trojena, Shura Island branded residences (Four Seasons / SLS / Jumeirah / Mandarin), Bvlgari, Six Senses, Aman, Baccarat, Raffles, Chedi, Corinthia, Ritz-Carlton Diriyah, and the Sindalah branded units all returned zero direct sales-driven Meta ads in Saudi Arabia in the period.

Recommendations

What Diriyah should do in the luxury segment

  1. Fix the disclaimer breakage on Diriyah Company’s own page.

    Four creatives reaching audiences above one million stopped for a compliance gap. The cost is not a re-shoot — it is a one-off review with the legal team to update the standing required-disclaimer text and re-publish at minimum the four affected creatives.

  2. Steal DarGlobal’s playbook for the silent operators.

    DarGlobal’s Amara at Rayana push has roughly 29 creative variants — architecture renders, family lifestyle, Arabic and English versions, vertical and square ratios, member-only-club trophy framing. That template can be replicated by the Aman, Baccarat, Raffles, Chedi, Corinthia, and Ritz-Carlton residences. The operators have the assets; what is missing is a buy-side party running the media. Diriyah Company can either run those campaigns under its own page, or coordinate with the operators’ holding teams.

  3. Match Red Sea Global’s launch-cadence discipline on Armani Residences.

    RSG ran the Nammos at AMAALA launch as a coordinated burst (multiple creatives, two languages, three or more ratios, a launch-week run starting April 27, 2026). Armani Residences in Diriyah deserve the same. Right now there is one sales creative; build a six-creative launch wave for the next sales phase, mirror the RSG cadence, and a/b test architecture vs. lifestyle vs. service-promise framing.

  4. Use Christie’s Real Estate Saudi as a templated broker channel.

    Christie’s KSA is already producing high-quality Rayana broker creatives (Apr 2026 wave: ~8 active variants, English and Arabic, both video and stills). They are also pushing Amaya in Jeddah. The same agency relationship can carry creatives for any of the silent Diriyah operators — the broker-side execution is in place.

  5. Distinguish Wadi Safar from the rest of the master plan in copy.

    The current Wadi Safar narrative blends “master development,” “members-only club,” “golf,” and “family lifestyle” at the same time. Tighten this into two parallel creatives: one for the trophy-asset buyer (Rayana Mansions), one for the family-lifestyle buyer (Amara). DarGlobal already runs both — the question is whether Diriyah Company’s own page should amplify the family-lifestyle line or stay in heritage mode.

  6. Set up a quarterly luxury-only benchmark.

    This report is a snapshot. The campaign cadence in luxury KSA is moving fast (RSG’s Nammos launch is two weeks old; DarGlobal’s Amara push is also fresh). A scheduled quarterly scrape of the same nine ecosystems plus a watch on the silent operators would give the marketing team early signal on competitor launches without re-doing the audit each time.

Methodology

How this report was assembled

Sources, scope, and counting conventions
  • Primary source: Meta Ad Library, Saudi Arabia geo, all formats, captured via headless Chromium / Playwright. Each card screenshot above is the live ad-card DOM element captured on 2026-05-06.
  • Geo: All counts and creatives are SA-targeted only. Globally targeted creatives that may include KSA in the audience pool are not counted unless directly visible in the SA Ad Library results.
  • Period: 2025-11-06 → 2026-05-06, six months. Active and inactive ads both counted; pre-period creatives still active are kept; pre-period creatives that ended before 2025-11-06 are excluded.
  • Variant definition: Each unique creative tied to one campaign is one variant. “This ad has multiple versions” on Meta is counted as 2 unless the actual version count is visible. “N ads use this creative and text” is counted as N.
  • Excluded: NHC and the Saudi mass-market ecosystem (Tamkean, Dar Wa Emaar, Mountain View SA, Retal, Al Tahaluf, Sharafa) — covered in the prior benchmark, out of scope here. Hospitality-only creatives (book-a-stay) without ownership / sales messaging are excluded.
  • Caveats: Meta Ad Library results pages are sometimes capped at a few hundred records per query; rare creatives may be missed at the long tail. Some keyword searches return cross-language false positives (Pakistan banking, Christian missions, Chinese state media) — those are filtered by hand and not counted.
  • Cross-channel not measured: Google Ads, TikTok Commercial Content Library, OOH, TV, podcasts, broker WhatsApp, sales-center direct outreach. ROSHN’s actual luxury reach is likely larger when those channels are included.
